newsitem.title: USA: Panel clears budget accord, sent to full House.
newsitem.headline: Panel clears budget accord, sent to full House.

text.p: The House Budget Committee Friday approved the fiscal 1998 budget resolution which embodies the balanced budget accord reached between the White House and congressional leaders on Thursday.
The full House will consider the budget plan Tuesday. The measure cleared the panel on a bipartisan vote of 31-7. All votes against it were cast by Democrats.

The budget cleared the committee without any significant changes to the agreement reached with the White House. The Senate Budget Committee will vote on an identical agreement Monday and easy approval is expected.
The budget agreement brings the federal budget to balance over the next five years by reining in spending for some expensive domestic programs, such as Medicare health care for the elderly.

It also provides a net tax cut of $85 billion through 2002 aimed at giving families tax breaks for education and children, cutting capital gains tax rates, expansion of individual retirement accounts and reductions in inheritance taxes.

President Clinton has praised the accord and Republican leaders say they also believe it will ease political strife over the budget. However, legislation needed to enact the savings and tax cuts will be hard fought.
